battle.name: 第一次卡洛斯戰爭
battle.theater: 西班牙北部納瓦拉與巴斯克地區
battle.brief: 第一次卡洛斯戰爭是戰爭列表所列的西班牙內戰，起因是王位繼承。1833年費爾南多七世去世後，卡洛斯派支持唐·卡洛斯爭位，伊莎貝二世一方由政府軍支持。戰事集中於北部納瓦拉、巴斯克及埃布羅河流域；野砲（Field gun）1550年已列裝，參與前線壓制與進攻支援。

kit.name: 野砲
kit.history: 能拆成幾件馬車拉走的砲。它讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火。

countries: 交戰的兩方是卡洛斯派與自由派。卡洛斯派以北方傳統主義省份為核心，即納瓦拉，以及巴斯克的阿拉瓦、比斯開、吉普斯夸三省，另加加泰隆尼亞與巴倫西亞由教會動員起來的鄉村武裝；其戰鬥骨幹是本地農莊民兵、教區神甫與修院武裝，基層多為漁民、走私者與熟悉山徑的獵人，軍官則大量來自自由派軍中倒戈者。自由派方面由攝政政府在馬德里直接掌握，以正規軍為骨架，配以民兵與皇家志願兵的徵召；一八三四年英國、法國、西班牙、葡萄牙簽訂四國同盟之後，又有英國輔助軍團、法國外籍軍團、葡萄牙輔助師，以及比利時與荷蘭的志願兵進駐北方。外籍部隊多集中在要道、守城與攻城方向，卡洛斯派則依靠本省徵集與山區遊擊維持戰力，雙方在埃布羅河中游一帶與北部山區拉鋸六年九個月，沒有任何一方能在野戰中速戰速決。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Carlists and the Liberals. The Carlist side was built on the traditionalist provinces of the north: Navarre, and the three Basque provinces of Alava, Biscay and Guipuzcoa, together with village militias in Catalonia and Valencia roused by the parish clergy. Its military backbone was the local farming militia, the armed men of the parishes and of religious houses, and the rank and file were drawn from fishermen, smugglers and hunters who knew the mountain paths, while many of its officers were deserters from the Liberal army. On the Liberal side the regency government in Madrid held the reins directly, resting on the regular army supplemented by the militia and by recruiting royal volunteers; after the Quadruple Alliance between Britain, France, Spain and Portugal was signed in 1834, the British Auxiliary Legion, the French Foreign Legion, the Portuguese Auxiliary Division and volunteers from Belgium and the Netherlands also arrived in the north. The foreign contingents were concentrated on the roads, in garrison duty and on siege operations, while the Carlists sustained their strength through provincial recruitment and mountain guerrilla warfare. The two sides fought a see-saw struggle for six years and nine months along the middle Ebro and across the northern mountains, and neither of them could achieve a quick decision in open battle.
people: 卡洛斯·德·波旁，即唐·卡洛斯，是費爾南多七世的弟弟，一八三三年十月二日在潘普洛納大教堂宣誓即位。攝政王后瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜以女王伊莎貝二世的名義執政：費爾南多七世於一八三三年九月二十九日病逝，遺囑所頒的《聖特莫制裁令》把王位限定在女嗣一系，正是卡洛斯派起兵的導火索。北方戰線真正的統帥是巴斯克工程師出身的托馬斯·祖馬拉卡雷吉，他自一八三四年起把鬆散的遊擊隊整頓成有紀律、能宿營、能行軍的部隊，並在一八三五年的阿爾拉班與維亞爾德洛斯納瓦羅斯以砲兵配合佯退擊敗自由派；同年七月的門迪戈里亞，他是敗方，十一月廿六日在潘普洛納因傷重去世，繼任者拉法埃爾·馬羅托後來轉向政府，並於一八三九年二月二日與埃斯帕特羅簽訂《維加拉公約》。自由派方面最重要的大將是巴爾多梅羅·埃斯帕特羅，他在一八三五年七月十六日的門迪戈里亞取得決定性勝利，之後主持北方戰區，並以一八四○年的公約了結殘局；佩德羅·阿古斯丁·希隆（阿胡馬達公爵）、何塞·德拉孔查與路易斯·德·奧多尼爾先後統軍。外籍指揮官方面，英國輔助軍團的萊西·埃文斯，以及法國外籍軍團的羅居、戈埃與蓋布里昂上校，在自由派陣線中承擔了最艱苦的山地與攻城任務。
peopleEn: Carlos de Borbon, known as Don Carlos, was the brother of Ferdinand VII and took the oath as king in the cathedral of Pamplona on the second of October 1833. The regent Maria Cristina governed in the name of Queen Isabella II: Ferdinand VII had died on the twenty-ninth of September 1833, and the Pragmatica Sanction issued in his will restricted the crown to the female line, which was the spark that set the Carlists in motion. The real commander of the northern front was Tomas de Zumalacarregui, a Basque engineer who from 1834 disciplined loose guerrilla bands into troops that could bivouac, march and fight in line, and who won at Arlaban and at Villar de los Navarros in 1835 by pairing artillery with a feigned retreat. He was the defeated party at Mendigorría in July of that year and died of his wounds at Pamplona on the twenty-sixth of November; his successor Rafael Maroto eventually went over to the government and signed the Convention of Vergara with Espartero on the second of February 1839. For the Liberals the indispensable commander was Baldomero Espartero, who won the decisive victory at Mendigorría on the sixteenth of July 1835, directed the northern theatre afterwards, and closed the war out with the convention of 1840; Pedro Agustin Giron, Duke of Ahumada, Jose de la Concha and Luis de Odonnel commanded in turn. Among the foreign commanders, George de Lacy Evans of the British Auxiliary Legion and Roguet, Goethals and Colonel Guebriant of the French Foreign Legion carried the hardest mountain and siege tasks inside the Liberal lines.
kits: 卡面的野砲是十六世紀中葉西班牙野戰砲的典型型態：鑄造的身管、滑膛的砲口，能拆成砲身、砲架與附件數件，分乘數輛馬車，由數匹至二十餘匹馬拖行。這套可以拆成幾件馬車拉走的形制，正是卡洛斯五世時期西班牙砲兵在帕維亞一役及其後數次義大利戰役中建立起來的野戰火力機制，讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火：砲數、射程、射速與齊射時機都能事先排定。一八三三年時，這門一五五○年的砲本身早已退役，但它確立的制度以另一副面貌延續下去。自由派使用十二磅、八磅與四磅的滑膛野砲，以及可以拆成三件、由驃馬馱運上山的山砲；卡洛斯派大量使用北方城防上原有的青銅砲改裝的野砲，單是阿爾拉班一役就集中了十餘門四磅山砲。火器方面，自由派以英國運來的燧發滑膛步槍為主，英國輔助軍團並配發來福槍；卡洛斯派則多為自備或由走私渠道入境的燧發步槍，另有短管霰彈槍與大砍刀。攻城與後勤同樣是裝備競賽的一環：貝尼托·佩雷斯要塞前線的攻城重砲、堵塞街道的柴車，以及以驃馬與牛車馱運糧秣給養的隊伍，構成了這場內戰的物資底層。
kitsEn: The field gun on the card is the typical form of the Spanish field piece of the mid sixteenth century: a cast barrel with a smooth bore, capable of being broken down into the barrel, the carriage and the accessories, which were carried on a number of wagons and drawn by anything from a few horses to more than twenty. This form, which could be taken apart and moved on several carts, was precisely the field system established by Spanish artillery under Charles V at Pavia and in the Italian campaigns that followed, and it was what gave field warfare its first calculable artillery fire: the number of pieces, the range, the rate of fire and the moment of the salvo could all be settled in advance. By 1833 the gun of 1550 itself was long out of service, but the system it had established survived in another guise. The Liberals used smoothbore field pieces of twelve, eight and four pounds, together with mountain guns that could be split into three loads and carried up on muleback; the Carlists used large numbers of old bronze pieces from the northern fortresses converted into field guns, and at Arlaban alone they concentrated more than ten four-pounder mountain guns. In small arms the Liberals relied mainly on flintlock smoothbore muskets brought from Britain, and the British Auxiliary Legion was issued rifles; the Carlists had mostly their own flintlock muskets or arms that came in by smuggling, together with short barrelled blunderbusses and heavy sabres. Siege and logistics were an equipment race in their own right: the heavy siege guns in front of the citadel of Bilbao, the faggots of timber used to block streets, and the mule and ox trains that carried food and ammunition formed the material base of this civil war.
tactics: 卡洛斯派的戰術核心是山區遊擊與正規野戰的混合。村鎮結社擔任據點守禦，遊擊隊切斷道路、伏擊護送隊與驛站，祖馬拉卡雷吉則把這些隊伍整頓成能行軍、能宿營、能就地取糧的軍隊，作戰上善用佯退、伏擊與居高臨下的砲兵配置：在阿爾拉班，他以十餘門四磅山砲封住維多利亞通往奧爾多堡的山道，讓自由派縱隊在風雪中擠成一團；在維亞爾德洛斯納瓦羅斯，他用砲火掩護假退卻，等自由派縱隊拉長到十數公里才以主力火砲回擊，隨即以騎兵切斷退路。自由派的打法較為死板：以線式縱隊與密集步兵配合火砲齊射正面硬推，力求速戰速決，並在冬季收縮封鎖線，試圖切斷北方的煤、鹽與槍彈流入；其弱點是徵召兵員訓練不足，冬季給養與傷病處理笨拙，一遇到山區消耗戰就容易拖成僵局。攻城戰中雙方都倚重近迫射擊、壕溝與攻城塔的配合，以及用石彈與火藥削弱城牆。
tacticsEn: The Carlist tactical core was a mixture of mountain guerrilla warfare and regular field combat. Village societies provided the strongpoints, guerrilla bands cut roads and ambushed convoys and relay stations, and Zumalacarregui turned those bands into an army that could march, bivouac and live off the country. In battle he relied on the feigned retreat, the ambush and the massing of artillery on high ground: at Arlaban he shut the mountain road from Vitoria to Orduna with more than ten four-pounder mountain guns and forced the Liberal column to bunch up in the snowstorm; at Villar de los Navarros he covered the pretended withdrawal with gunfire, waited until the Liberal column had stretched out over ten kilometres, brought his heavy guns to bear on it and sent cavalry to cut the road back. The Liberal method was stiffer: line columns and close infantry supported by salvo fire were pushed straight ahead in the hope of a quick decision, and in winter the blockade lines were tightened in an effort to cut off coal, salt and ammunition flowing into the north. The weakness of that method was badly trained conscript infantry, clumsy winter supply and an indifferent handling of the sick and wounded, which turned a mountain war of attrition into a stalemate. In siege operations both sides relied on close fire, on trenches and on the combination of siege towers and towers for the walls, weakening masonry with stone shot and powder.
data: 戰爭自一八三三年十月二日至一八四○年七月，前後六年九個月。會戰數字各方記載不一，只能取其大略：一八三五年一月的阿爾拉班，卡洛斯派以數千之眾與十餘門四磅山砲封住山道，自由派縱隊遠多於此卻在風雪中受挫；同年三月十七日的維亞爾德洛斯納瓦羅斯，卡洛斯軍以假退與集中砲火擊潰遠多於己的縱隊，自由派損失以千計；同年七月十六日的門迪戈里亞，埃斯帕特羅所部常被引為約一萬二千人，卡洛斯軍約七千人，祖馬拉卡雷吉重傷，卡洛斯軍損失慘重。英國輔助軍團最多時約七千人，法國外籍軍團約三千五百人，葡萄牙輔助師約六千人，均為常見引述之數。外籍兵員與直接從國外輸入的槍械彈藥，在一八三五年至一八三七年最受北方的歡迎，英法聯軍封鎖線所切的貝爾梅奧與帕薩亞兩港，是這段補給競賽的關鍵節點。
dataEn: The war ran from the second of October 1833 to July 1840, six years and nine months in all. The figures for the battles differ from one account to another and can only be given approximately: at Arlaban in January 1835 the Carlists blocked the mountain road with several thousand men and more than ten four-pounder mountain guns, and a Liberal column far larger than that was checked in the snowstorm; at Villar de los Navarros on the seventeenth of March of the same year the Carlist army broke a column much stronger than itself by a feigned retreat and massed gunfire, the Liberal losses running into the thousands; at Mendigorría on the sixteenth of July Espartero's army is commonly given as about twelve thousand men against some seven thousand Carlists, Zumalacarregui being badly wounded and the Carlist losses heavy. The British Auxiliary Legion numbered about seven thousand at its peak, the French Foreign Legion about three thousand five hundred and the Portuguese Auxiliary Division about six thousand, all figures that are frequently cited. Foreign personnel and arms imported directly from abroad were most welcome in the north between 1835 and 1837, and the ports of Bermeo and Pasajes sealed by the Anglo-French blockade line were the decisive point of that supply race.
cause: 一八三三年九月二十九日費爾南多七世病逝，遺囑所頒的《聖特莫制裁令》援引塞維利亞王位繼承法典，宣布由年僅三歲的女兒伊莎貝二世繼承，妻瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜攝政。此舉同時觸動三件事：巴斯克與納瓦拉各省依福爾洛斯享有的地方軍役、稅制與司法特權；教會的產業、修院與傳統影響；以及自由派政府擴編常備軍、逐步干預教會的趨勢。教會界、大部分軍官與鄉村紳士因此倒向王弟卡洛斯，北方三省的徵兵與稅務衝突更成為直接的導火索。法國一八三○年七月革命之後席捲歐洲的自由主義與立憲風潮，令年輕的卡洛斯派得以自居立憲派之名；外國同情者提供的資金、走私流入的槍械與已成熟的遊擊經驗，則讓零星起事得以蔓延。最終一切匯聚於一八三三年十月二日潘普洛納的宣誓，一場為王位而起的內戰在西班牙北部全面鋪開。
causeEn: Ferdinand VII died on the twenty-ninth of September 1833, and the Pragmatica Sanction contained in his will invoked the Castilian law of succession to declare that the crown should pass to his three-year-old daughter Isabella II, with his widow Maria Cristina as regent. That single act touched three things at once: the local military service, taxation and judicial privileges the Basque provinces and Navarre held under their fueros; the property, religious houses and traditional influence of the Church; and the Liberal government's drive to enlarge the standing army and to encroach on ecclesiastical property. The clergy, most of the officer corps and the rural gentry therefore turned to the king's brother, and the quarrels over recruitment and taxation in the three northern provinces became the immediate spark. The wave of liberalism and constitutionalism that swept Europe after the French revolution of July 1830 allowed the young Carlists to present themselves as the constitutional party, while money from foreign sympathisers, arms arriving by smuggling and guerrilla experience already gathered in the field let scattered risings spread. All of it came together in the oath sworn at Pamplona on the second of October 1833, and a civil war fought over the crown opened across the north of Spain.
impact: 第一次卡洛斯戰爭重塑了西班牙十九世紀。以王位為名的內戰並沒有解決王位問題，卻把卡洛斯主義變成長壽的政治運動，其後還有一八四六至一八四九年、一八七二至一八七六年的兩場戰爭，直到二十世紀仍有餘波。自由派為此建立了全國性的常備軍與財政體系，巴斯克與納瓦拉的特權爭議則被推遲而非消除。對歐洲軍事觀察者而言，這是一場示範近代砲兵、遊擊與正規戰如何互相牽制的沙盤：萊西·埃文斯所寫的英國輔助軍團戰後檢討書，以及比利時、德國志願者的報告，都被廣泛翻譯流傳；四國同盟干預與封鎖北方的做法，也成為此後歐洲干涉西班牙內政的先例。西班牙在歐洲的孤立由此加深，承認需要外國兵力平叛，等於公開自己的軍備與財政無力，國家近代化被推遲，往後數十年仍靠外來借款維持軍隊。
impactEn: The First Carlist War reshaped nineteenth-century Spain. A civil war fought over a crown did not settle the question of the crown, but it turned Carlism into a durable political movement, followed by two further wars in 1846 to 1849 and 1872 to 1876, with echoes running into the twentieth century. The Liberals built a national standing army and a national fiscal system in response, while the quarrel over Basque and Navarrese privileges was postponed rather than settled. For European military observers it was a proving ground showing how modern artillery, guerrilla war and regular battle held one another in check: the after-action report written by Lacy Evans on the British Auxiliary Legion, and the reports of Belgian and German volunteers, were widely translated and circulated, and the intervention of the Quadruple Alliance with the blockade of the northern coast became a precedent for later European interference in Spanish civil politics. Spain's isolation in Europe deepened accordingly. Admitting that foreign troops were needed to put down a rebellion was a public admission of military and financial incapacity, and modernisation of the state was postponed, the army still being maintained in later decades on foreign credit.
result: 一八四○年七月，卡洛斯派殘部依《維加拉公約》放下武器，六年九個月的戰爭以雙方妥協收場：自由派保住王位與國家統一，北方三省的福爾洛斯獲得部分保留，阿拉瓦與比斯開的稅制與若干地方特權獲得承認；卡洛斯派則換得體面退場，協議明定不得因過去的信仰與政治立場而迫害對方軍人。卡洛斯本人流亡，先後居於葡萄牙、法國與德國，一八七八年病逝國外，卡洛斯主義卻作為政治反對派與宗教鬥爭延續下去。戰爭的後果也寫進了西班牙的軍政：以王位為名的內戰結束後，自由派企圖用常備軍、外籍軍團與海軍封鎖建立秩序，卻同時把軍隊變成決定政治的集團；一八四○年之後的埃斯帕特羅攝政、一八四一年的倒台、一八四三年伊莎貝二世加冕，以及此後溫和派與激進派的分裂，幾乎都源於這場戰爭留下的軍隊與派系。
resultEn: In July 1840 the remaining Carlist forces laid down their arms under the Convention of Vergara, and six years and nine months of war ended in a compromise on both sides: the Liberals kept the crown and the unity of the country, and the fueros of the three northern provinces were in part preserved, with the fiscal arrangements and certain local privileges of Alava and Biscay acknowledged; the Carlists bought a dignified exit, and the convention barred either side from punishing the soldiers of the other for past religious or political positions. Don Carlos himself went into exile, living at various times in Portugal, France and Germany and dying abroad in 1878, while Carlism itself went on as a political opposition and a religious struggle. The consequences were written into the military and political life of Spain: once a war over the crown was over, the Liberals tried to establish order with a standing army, foreign contingents and a naval blockade, and in doing so made the army a group that decided politics. Espartero's regency of 1840 and his fall in 1841, the coronation of Isabella II in 1843, and the later split between the moderates and the progressives all grew out of the army and the factions this war left behind.
